Solar Activity:
 Low activity is likely, but with a chance of rising to Moderate due to isolated Moderate-class flares.



Solar Wind / Geomagnetic Activity: 
Two weak, slow, and faint CMEs may deliver glancing impacts early on Day 1 (30 July), and again late Day 2 (31 July). However, both CMEs are considered more likely to mostly miss Earth. Otherwise, Background slow winds conditions are expected to largely prevail, with only a slight enhancement possible from any fast wind of the southern coronal hole, which is expected to pass mostly south of Earth. Quiet activity is generally expected, with isolated Unsettled spells, but also a chance of Active intervals from any CME glance or fast wind enhancement.



Energetic Particles / Solar Radiation: 
The count rate of energetic particles (high energy protons) is most likely to remain at background with no Solar Radiation storms occurring.
